answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers correlated penalties growing as O(k²), not as independent linear fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling stake, rapidly exhausting a swarm’s economic base through asymmetric depreciation. A bridge, prism, or sparrow identity therefore cannot cheaply mask common control or make attacks profitable.
